l: (Joan looks up over her half-moon glasses, a telephone tucked under her chin.) Well, look who's back. Chuck's had me watching the door since seven. (She puts the telephone down.) How was the leave? No, don't tell me. You'll only make me jealous.

You too. Nothing changes: Chuck's upstairs, the coffee's still terrible, and Doris wants you in the Cover Story Department first, through the door on the left. Wherever he's sending you, you're not going as yourself.
(Joan doesn't stop typing.) You know the way: Cover Story's through the door on the left, Chuck's up the stairs, and the coffee's in the cafeteria. I still wouldn't.
(Peggy grins.) Back for more? I'm flying you, wherever it is. We're not going anywhere until Chuck's had his talk with you, upstairs. Then she's all yours.
My name is Chuck. I work at Chuck's Office. I like CIA.
(Doris looks you up and down.) You again. Sit down, let's have a look at you. Hair, clothes, the lot: wherever Chuck's sending you this time, you're not going in a government suit.

There you are. Sit down. Good to have you back. Like the new look. You're going to Sarivalto, an island in the Baltic. Snow, fish, cola and not much else. Its king has just died, and right now nobody knows who's going to run the place.

Everyone. The Communists want the island in the Soviet Union, and Moscow would love a harbour that far north. The royals want the crown kept on Prince Leopold's head. Kelp Cola wants whoever's best for business. The Democrats want a vote. And there's an oil company and a syndicate sniffing around too.

An island that doesn't end up flying a red flag. Your codename is NIGHTJAR. Your cover's a British reporter, from a London paper, there to cover the king's death, so ask all the questions you like. When you're settled in, go and introduce yourself to the island's newspaper, the Eastbrook Gazette: a reporter would. Our man there is Hekki, the radio tech: he's fixed you up a room under his shack, at the radio tower, with a radio set and a screen to reach me on.
You fly out for the first of September, and the island's yours for thirty days. Talk to everyone, help the people who'll help us, and call me every morning. Good luck, NIGHTJAR.
Me again: I'm your ride. It's a long way to the Baltic, and we don't land anywhere anyone can see: a fishing boat meets us off the island at dawn and takes you the rest of the way in. Ready?
(Sam is mending a net on an upturned crate. He nods.) Reporter.
My father's. He knotted it in 1931. I'm mending it. A knot at a time.
(Kaisa slides the headphones off one ear.) Radio Sarivalto, live and slightly out of tune. I'm Kaisa. You're the reporter, the whole island's heard. Don't touch the red button.
Everyone. Communists, monks, oil men. It's the only thing we agree on.
(Hekki looks both ways along the path, twice.) You're NIGHTJAR. You must be. You look exactly like a British reporter, which is the idea, I suppose. I'm Hekki. Radio. And, well. The other thing.
(He drops to a whisper.) Sorry. Sorry. I've been practising. Your room's under my shack: the bookcase, third shelf. Lean on it. It swings.

Radio sets, tape recorders, a bed, a stove, and more tinned soup than one person needs. And the radio set, for calling Chuck: tune it in and call him the minute you're down there. He'll want to hear you've landed. (He swallows.) Welcome to Sarivalto, NIGHTJAR.
"Sorry, I can't think straight. You don't have any food on you, do you?" you ask. Then you've come to the right person. Have a look at what I've got.
(Chuck's voice, thin through the static.) NIGHTJAR, Langley. Good to hear you. Did you make it in one piece?
In one piece. Hekki says hello.

Good. First job: the Communist Party. They want this island in the Soviet Union, and that's exactly what we're here to stop. Their leader is a woman called Anna, at their HQ in Saltwick. Go and talk to her. Friendly. Find out where they stand, and don't tip your hand. Over.
Comrade! Not many come in from the cold to visit us. What brings you to the Party's door?
A journalist! Then write this down: Sarivalto's future lies with the Soviet Union. Moscow will give this island what its kings never did.
NIGHTJAR. You saw Anna? What's the Party really after?
She wants the island in the Soviet Union, and she means it.
That's what I was afraid of. A true believer's harder to deal with than a man with a price. Good work. Get some sleep: tomorrow, Kingsgrad.
(Tiina doesn't look up.) Sirpa's told you everything already, I expect. She'll have told you my name's Tiina. That's all you need to know today.
Is it? You don't know me yet. Wait a week. (The corner of her mouth moves.)
Go on. Sirpa's got more to say than I have.
(Sirpa looks you up and down.) Well! You came in on Tom's boat this morning. Don't look like that: I see everything that comes up this street. Sirpa. And you're the reporter.
Anna's had the Party lights on since five, Lucia came home at three in the morning with sand on her shoes, and Hannu's selling last week's paper again.
(Ray looks you up and down, the way she looks at everyone, and then puts a glass on the bar.) You're the first stranger through that door since the snow came. What'll it be?
Whisky, then. It's the only thing in Saltwick that's been warm since August.
